items.title: J. Leo Rayhill interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 23, 2007
items.q: I remember after Gene Romano was one of my dearest friends in the whole world

ctx.x: Oh okay. I’ll be darned. What about the alcohol policy at that time?

It was open. You’d get away with anything we did. It was great. I remember after Gene Romano was one of my dearest friends in the whole world, he had a milk can full of whiskey sours and he’d carry it around party to party, great times, great times.
That’s great. But the fraternities, people who were at Hamilton at that time, they usually speak pretty highly of the fraternity system.
